title: In 40 CMIP6 runs the North Pacific winter outcrop of sigma0 26.4-26.7 is too small in 23; its size predicts age, AOU and O2 on 26.5 off California; WOA23 shows a 61% loss no run matches
abstract: Question: why do CMIP6 models miss the observed oxygen (O2) loss on the sigma0 26.5 kg/m3 surface off California, and where does this water get its O2? Approach: we measured the late-winter (January-April maximum) outcrop of the 26.4-26.7 density class in the open North Pacific in World Ocean Atlas 2023 decadal fields (1955-2022) and in 40 CMIP6 historical runs (1950-2014). For 13 runs we put model temperature, salinity, ideal age and O2 on sigma0 26.5 and compared them across models with the outcrop size. Results: in WOA23 the outcrop area fell by 61% (26.4-26.7) and by 86% (sigma0 >= 26.5) from 1965-1984 to 2005-2022, as March surface water at 38-48 N, 150-170 E became 0.16 kg/m3 lighter. In 23 of 40 runs the 1985-2014 outcrop was below 25% of WOA23; all 23 have March surface water that is too light (median bias -0.27 kg/m3; most too warm and too fresh). Across runs, a larger outcrop went with more O2 at the CalCOFI box on sigma0 26.5 (Spearman +0.72, n = 10, p = 0.011; families +0.82), lower AOU (-0.67), younger ideal age (-0.66, n = 13; families not significant) and a shallower 26.5 surface. All 10 tested runs had less O2 there than WOA23 (6-99 vs 105 umol/kg). In the seven runs with a real outcrop, the 2005-2014/1965-1984 outcrop ratio was 0.73-0.97, against 0.39 observed. Cross-model change and single-run lag tests were inconclusive, and a planned multi-member test was stopped by a slow network. Conclusion: most CMIP6 models do not ventilate sigma0 26.5 through a North Pacific outcrop, and those that do lose too little outcrop; both limit the model O2 response. The cross-model relation is a mean-state result from few runs, not proof of cause.

citations.reason: We confirm its outcrop shrinkage with public WOA23 fields and extend its single-member CMIP6 outcrop check to 40 runs with model age and O2 on sigma0 26.5.
We use its annual CMIP6 samples on sigma0 26.5 and give a ventilation reason why models change O2 less than observed.
We use its GFDL-ESM4 April samples and explain part of the model-observation O2 gap at CalCOFI.
We show its WOD band O2 series against the WOA23 outcrop record.
Its within-water-type loss is consistent with a ventilation source at the northwestern Pacific outcrop.
Tracer-age attribution of the sigma0 26.5 AOU changes.
Float evidence of continued offshore O2 loss on sigma0 26.5.
Float evidence for the offshore source of the CalCOFI low.
